analysis: Reading of the question: the author asks how the maintenance mechanism (th_maintenance, Keeping the channels) can develop across ten Books without repeating itself. The candidate develops Books 1-30 but leaves Books 22-30 largely open, so I take the ten Books to be 21-30, starting from the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion. The candidate records no current frontier, so this is an assumption. Current shape: the recorded thread already runs one full cycle. The Lowfen channel breaks (Book 19), few-hands households cannot cover it, lineage crews repair it under a Special Draw Right (Book 20), and one household declines and its water runs wild down the lowest Lowfen terrace (Book 21). The Long Return then needs channel labour again before its Book 30 date. If the thread continues in this form it risks one template: shortfall, rota dispute, refusal, physical damage on the lowest terrace, council response. On this reading the repetition comes from the template rather than from the subject. Where variation can come from: the mechanism is built from separable variables, and changing one of them for each stretch of Books gives a different dramatic problem without adding a new engine. (1) The scarce resource, which is hands in Arc IV, can become skill (who can still read and repair the channels) or a type of work (repair of what existed, versus construction of capacity the pulse needs). (2) The locus of consequence, which is the decliner's own terrace in the recorded link, can move to neighbours or a shared reach. (3) Visibility: the ledger's revision records the hours each hand worked beside its mark, so labour can be read and not only counted. (4) The agent of maintenance can pass between lineage crews, rota households, the Compact's grain-labour and the Gate Table. Changing only the rota's terms, the tone or the setting would reallocate the same cost, which is decoration rather than development. Suggested sequencing, offered for testing and not decided: Books 23-26 can move scarcity from hands to skill as the Brightwater generation assumes abundance needs no work, with the lineage's apprenticeship condition as the pressure point. Books 27-29 can let the Compact's offer and any ratification window raise who pays for repair. Book 30 then chooses among A, B and C while the maintenance thread is still open, so the finale is not pre-empted. Each path should be checked against the recorded failure modes of A, B and C so that it supports the choice without deciding it. Constraints: the composition values (complexity, causal distribution, engine hierarchy) are not declared, so the hypotheses assume no single-centre or ensemble structure. Hypothesis 2 changes the meaning of the recorded Book 21 link and must enter as a later pattern or as an account of Book 21, not as a silent rewrite. These are literary interpretations; the graph proves none of the causal claims, and nothing here is accepted canon or an ArchitectureCandidate.

recorded_observations.claim: Recorded thread: who performs the return labour that keeps the spring balanced, and at what cost to families with few hands. Old lineages hold repair skill from Books 9-11; from Book 20 lineage crews carry channel repair under a Special Draw Right while households that can meet the rota carry the rest. In this reading, the current form invites one repeating template.

Recorded: a declined share runs wild down the lowest Lowfen terrace (str_declined_share to str_lowfen_channel). It is the only recorded link from a declined share to physical damage, so a later refusal would repeat it unless the cause changes.

Recorded: lineage crews carry channel repair from Book 20 (inst_lineage_crews to th_maintenance). The Special Draw Right gives skill a claim on draw, and whether that Right is revocable by the Council is still open, so the lineage's standing depends on a condition not yet settled.

Recorded: a deep-store pulse in Book 30, predicted by the Balance Stones from Book 23. It needs channel labour before its date and a Gate schedule that routes it, and the routing choice belongs to the valley. This suggests a single large labour obligation rather than the seasonal rota.

Recorded: maintenance lineages hold the knowledge needed to read the stones (pastoral reinforces mystery). The recorded risk is that this knowledge hardens into hereditary privilege, so any path that moves scarcity to skill meets that risk first.

Recorded aesthetic strategy: one named household and one season, rendered with its own reasons, for grief that a household's water is cut for hands it cannot return. This suggests each later shortfall could use a new household and season rather than the Book 21 case.

Recorded: Books 23-26 carry the Brightwater inheritance (abundance drawn unevenly, with a belief that abundance needs no work); Books 27-29 carry the Compact's bid and, under Alternative C, the ratification window; Book 30 chooses among three mechanisms for who gives labour and who is counted.

Open question (index 4): is the lineage Special Draw Right revocable or permanent, what training condition does it carry, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end? Not decided. The answer decides whether a skill-based path can harden into permanent privilege.

hypotheses.title: Scarcity moves from hands to skill (hypothesis)
hypotheses.description: Changes the causal variable from labour supply to the transmission of repair knowledge. In Books 23-26, under the Brightwater belief that abundance needs no work, the rota lapses in the seasonal surplus while the lineage crews age without apprentices. The physical failure becomes latent: a channel that no one can still read, rather than a declined share. It operates through the Special Draw Right's training condition. The decisive choice falls on the Terrace Council and the lineage: whether to keep the Right on condition of training outsiders, which pays lineages in draw to teach. The cost is either a lineage monopoly that hardens into hereditary privilege (the recorded gi_pastoral_mystery_reinforces risk), or a repair gap that Compact grain-labour can fill only on the Compact's terms. The reader must weigh trust in those who hold the knowledge against the danger that no one else does. This differs from Book 21 because the trigger is competence rather than refusal, and the crisis arrives late, in Books 27-29, when the Compact's offer makes the gap visible.

hypotheses.title: Consequence of refusal lands on neighbours (hypothesis)
hypotheses.description: Changes where the cost of an unreturned share lands. In the recorded wiring a declined share floods the decliner's own lowest terrace. Here the water from a declined share runs into a shared reach, the Lower Ammen wells, and the households who keep the rota must repair that reach with their own hands. Refusal stops being a private cost. The operating rule is that the physical consequence is spread across a reach, so a later refusal means something different: it asks neighbours to absorb a burden they did not choose. The decisive choice falls on rota-keeping households, who must either enforce the rota by a binding rule, close to Alternative B's mechanism, or accept the repair as a standing cost. The reader must weigh whether declining is a right or a harm to others, and the story has no villain to settle it. Because this path changes the recorded Book 21 link, it should enter as a later pattern or as the Council's own account of Book 21, not as a silent rewrite. It keeps the rota but changes the social scale of its failure, so repetition is avoided by changing who suffers rather than the rota's form.

hypotheses.title: From repairing what existed to building what the pulse needs (hypothesis)
hypotheses.description: Changes the kind of work, not only who does it. From Book 23 the labour moves from repairing the existing channels to building capacity the Long Return needs: a new channel or outlet that the Gate can route. The working candidate leaves the surge route, and the high cistern's storage above tolerance, open. The obligation becomes one large, time-bounded commitment before the Book 30 date, rather than a recurring seasonal rota. The operating rule: the Balance Stones' Book 23 prediction sets the size and deadline of the build, and the route decision determines where the labour must be found. The decisive choice falls on the Council and the Gate Table: build a route that is safer but needs lowland and Compact labour, or route the surge through existing channels at greater risk of flooding. The cost is that the chosen route concentrates labour where it is least spare, and the reader must weigh the losses of a flood against the people who must build the safer route. This path changes the time horizon and the shape of the obligation, so it does not repeat the seasonal refusal template. It remains compatible with A, B and C, since each can contain or refuse the build.

hypotheses.title: The record exposes uncounted labour (hypothesis)
hypotheses.description: Changes the thread's relation to the mystery genre. The ledger's revision now records the hours each hand worked beside its mark. Here a reading by the Reading Hall in Books 24-26 uses those hours to show that much of the Lowfen repair credited to the rota was done by unnamed hands, including apprentices from outside the lineage. The labour was real, but the rota's record is false. This applies the Book 1 pattern of falsified credit to maintenance. The operating rule: the revised ledger becomes an instrument of exposure, and who did the work becomes an investigation rather than a rota dispute. The decisive choice falls on the Reading Hall and the Terrace Council: publish the hours, which reveals shortfalls and may shame households that could not meet the rota, or keep them in the stewardship tally, which protects dignity but leaves the public record partly false. The reader must weigh visibility against dignity, and accuracy against the privacy of household shortfalls. The path reuses the mystery engine, so it must not repeat the Book 1 reveal exactly; the difference lies in the falsehood being about labour rather than credit.

uncertainties: The ten Books are read as Books 21-30; the candidate records no current frontier, so the starting point is an assumption.
Which finale mechanism (A, B, C or a third) the author chooses for labour and counting (q-finale-mechanism) determines which development paths stay coherent; none is pre-chosen here.
Whether the Special Draw Right is revocable or permanent, and on what training condition (q-right-revocable), controls whether a skill path can harden into hereditary privilege.
Whether the Hollow Gate and Gate Table are accepted parts of the world (q-gate-table) affects every path that routes labour or water through the Gate.
The Book 15 surfeit mechanism is agent-proposed and the author may reject it; the consequences of Books 21-30 depend on it.
Whether the ledger revision that records hours beside each mark is an intended author change or a working addition is not recorded; the fourth hypothesis depends on it.
The high cistern's storage above tolerance is not established (q-other-15), and the route options for the Long Return depend on it.
Whether repetition has been avoided is a reader-experience judgement that the graph cannot measure; the variation criteria here are design hypotheses, not proof.
